extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and applicants (practitioners) dealing with PCT international applications entering the U.S. national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for entering and prosecuting an international (PCT) application in the U.S. national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, including required papers, timing, priority/benefit claims, abandonment consequences, and examiner procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or declaration identifying the international application
rubrics_metrics.description: When entering the national stage after a declaration of inventorship was executed in the international application under PCT Rule 4.17(iv), applicant must submit either a new oath or declaration or an application data sheet (ADS) as set forth in 37 CFR 1.76 correctly identifying the application upon which priority is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants entering under 35 U.S.C. 371 for an international filing date prior to Sept. 16, 2012 must file an oath or declaration in accordance with pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.497(a)-(b). If the oath/declaration is missing after basic national fee and copy have been received by expiration of 30 months, USPTO sends a Notification of Missing Requirements (Form PCT/DO/EO/905) allowing time to correct defects and to submit required surcharge under 37 CFR 1.492(h). Failure to timely file the required oath/declaration will result in abandonment. An oath/declaration that complies with pre-AIA 1.497(a)-(b) suffices for national stage entry, but if it does not also meet 37 CFR 1.63 requirements, a supplemental oath/declaration or ADS (where permitted under 1.63(c)) must be submitted (see 37 CFR 1.497(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for supplemental oath/declaration or ADS when original fails additional requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If an oath/declaration submitted (including one under PCT Rule 4.17(iv)) does not comply with additional requirements for oaths/declarations set forth in 37 CFR 1.63, applicants must submit a supplemental oath/declaration or an ADS where permitted under 37 CFR 1.63(c) to correct the deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situations requiring supplemental submissions include changes in inventorship under PCT Rule 92bis, changes to international filing date under PCT Rule 20.5(c), or corrections/additions to priority claims under PCT Rule 26.2bis after execution of the PCT Rule 4.17(iv) declaration. See pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.497(f)(1)-(2) and 1.497(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship consistency and correction procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventorship of the national stage application is that set forth in the international application (including changes under PCT Rule 92bis). An oath/declaration naming an inventive entity different than that set forth in the international application will not be accepted unless inventorship is corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct inventorship by following pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.497(d) and 37 CFR 1.48(a). If an inventor refuses to sign or cannot be found after diligent effort, applicant may file an oath/declaration and a petition under pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.47. For deceased or incapacitated inventors, use pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.42 or 1.43. Discrepancies in inventor names between the international application and the oath/declaration require correction (use 37 CFR 1.48(f) effective Sept.16,2012 where available, otherwise petition under 37 CFR 1.182).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to meet national-stage submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If basic national fee and a copy of the international application are not submitted prior to the expiration of 30 months from the priority date, the international application becomes abandoned as to the United States (37 CFR 1.495(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative filing methods (hand-delivery, Priority Mail Express®) may be used if USPTO electronic filing is unavailable (37 CFR 1.10). If requirements under 37 CFR 1.495(b) are timely met but the requirements under 37 CFR 1.495(c) (e.g., English translation, oath/declaration, search fee, examination fee, application size fee) are not met within the time set by notice, the application will become abandoned upon expiration of that period. Papers deficient in fees (insufficient basic national fee amount) can cause abandonment. Applicant may petition to revive an abandoned application under 37 CFR 1.137 (see MPEP § 711.03(c)); form PTO/SB/64PCT may be used for convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution limits and advancement for certain international opinions/reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Once taken up by the examiner, national stage prosecution generally proceeds like a domestic application, except the international filing date (or priority date) is used for prior art search and unity of invention proceeds under 37 CFR 1.475.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National stage applications that paid required search and examination fees may be amended after commencement of national stage processing only to the extent necessary to eliminate objections as to form or to cancel rejected claims; such applications are advanced out of turn for examination. If an IPER or a written opinion by a U.S. ISA states novelty, inventive step (non-obviousness), and industrial applicability have been satisfied for all presented claims, national stage search and examination fees are reduced (see 37 CFR 1.492(b)(1), 1.492(c)(1)), the application may be amended only to eliminate form objections or cancel rejected claims, and it will be advanced out of turn. Examiners should bear in mind the international filing date (or priority date) when searching prior art and apply unity rules under 37 CFR 1.475.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of an initial submission as a 35 U.S.C. 371 national-stage filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s initial submission under 35 U.S.C. 371 must be identified as a submission to enter the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371; otherwise it will be treated as a filing under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) (unless clearly a 35 U.S.C. 154(d)(4) provisional-rights submission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable ways to identify the submission include selecting “371 National Stage” in the USPTO electronic filing system, using transmittal Form PTO-1390, or including an inventor’s oath/declaration that identifies the international application by international application number as the application to which the oath/declaration is directed. Notably, merely claiming priority of an international application in an oath/declaration does not indicate a submission under 35 U.S.C. 371. Examiners should check for Form PCT/DO/EO/903 (Notice of Acceptance of Application under 35 U.S.C. 371) and bib-data indications; if neither is present and no evidence indicates national-stage processing was desired, treat as a 111(a) filing. If both indications are present, treat as 371. For questions, consult International Patent Legal Administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling conflicting instructions about filing treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: When the initial submission contains conflicting instructions as to whether filing is under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or 35 U.S.C. 371, treat the application according to 37 CFR 1.495(g) (post-Sept.16,2012: conflicting indications result in treatment as a national stage submission under 35 U.S.C. 371).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of conflicting instructions: selecting 'Utility Nonprovisional' yet indicating 371 elsewhere; including both selection of 371 and a Utility Patent Application Transmittal (Form PTO/AIA/15 or PTO/SB/05); including a benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 120 to the international application while selecting a different submission type. Examiner should contact International Patent Legal Administration when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date vs. 371(c) (date of entry) distinction and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The international filing date is the filing date for both the international and national stages; however, the date of entry into the national stage (the '371(c) date')—not the international filing date—is used for taking up the national stage application for action and appears as the 'Filing or 371(c) Date' on filing receipts and Patent Data Portal entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PCT/DO/EO/903 indicates the 371(c) date. Because of AIA changes, the items that constitute fulfillment of 35 U.S.C. 371 for determining the 371(c) date depend on the international filing date (pre- vs post-Sept.16,2012). The MPEP lists the elements relevant to the 'Date of Completion of all 35 U.S.C. 371 Requirements' (A-G) used for patent-term adjustment calculations. Note the AIA Technical Corrections Act (Pub. Law 112-274) revised measurement for the 14-month PTA period to the date of commencement of the national stage under 371.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of priority: timely claiming and restoration options
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. national stage application may be entitled to a right of priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a) and 365(b) based on a prior foreign application or international application designating at least one country other than the U.S.; to obtain priority the priority must have been timely claimed in the international stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claim of foreign priority is not timely made in the international stage, a priority claim may be made in the U.S. national stage upon petition under 37 CFR 1.55(e) if the entire delay was unintentional. International applications filed on/after April 1, 2007 may have priority restored under amended PCT Rules (PCT Rule 26bis.3); restoration in the U.S. national stage may be obtained by petition under 37 CFR 1.55(c). Presentation of the priority claim in an ADS is permissible but not required; examiners should check for certified copies of priority documents forwarded by the International Bureau (see certified copy criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy of the priority document and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT Rule 17 requires a certified copy of the foreign priority application to be furnished (to the receiving Office or International Bureau) within 16 months from the priority date; the International Bureau normally forwards such certified copies to Designated Offices that request them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy from the International Bureau with an indication of compliance with PCT Rule 17.1(a)/(b)/(b-bis) is acceptable to establish compliance with 37 CFR 1.55(f); examiner should acknowledge receipt in the next Office action. If the International Bureau cannot forward a certified copy, the applicant must provide one during the national stage unless 37 CFR 1.55(h) or 1.55(i) apply. For national stage commencements on/after Dec.18,2013, applicant must submit the certified copy within the later of four months from the date of entry into the U.S. national stage (per 37 CFR 1.491) or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior-filed foreign application (see 37 CFR 1.55(f)(2)); delay may be excused by petition under 37 CFR 1.55(f)(3). If priority document wasn't provided in compliance with PCT Rule 17, the IB will not forward it; in cases of asserted timely furnishing where copy is missing from file, examiner should consult a Quality Assurance Specialist or PCT Special Program Examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit claims to prior U.S. provisional, nonprovisional, or international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A national stage application may include a benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) (provisional), or 120 and 365(c) (prior U.S. national or international applications). Conditions mirror those in MPEP §§ 201.07, 201.08, 211 et seq. and require compliance with 37 CFR 1.78 (and 1.78(d) for 120/365(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain benefit under 119(e), the national stage application must comply with 37 CFR 1.78(a): the prior provisional must be entitled to a filing date (37 CFR 1.53(c)), basic filing fee paid on provisional within required period (37 CFR 1.16(d)), the provisional must name at least one inventor named in the later international application, and the provisional must disclose the inventor’s invention claimed in at least one claim of the national stage app in the manner of 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph. The national stage application must reference the provisional by number (series code and serial) within the time in 1.78(a)(4). If the international filing date is prior to Sept.16,2012 the reference may be in ADS or first sentence(s) of specification; on/after Sept.16,2012 the reference must be in ADS (37 CFR 1.78(a)(3), pre-AIA 1.78(a)(5)(iii)). Translational requirements apply if provisional was non-English. Restoration of benefit or priority may be possible via petitions under 37 CFR 1.78(b) or 1.78(c) (and analogous 1.55 petitions where applicable). Failure to timely submit required references under 1.78(d)(3) for 120/365(c) is considered a waiver of benefit unless a petition for unintentional delay is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on claiming benefit to the same international application
rubrics_metrics.description: A national stage application submitted under 35 U.S.C. 371 may not claim benefit of the filing date of the international application of which it is the national stage since its filing date is the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the international application and the national stage share the same filing date, a benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 120 in the national stage to that international application is inappropriate. See related discussion in MPEP § 1893.03(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention requirement and election procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner finds the national stage application lacks unity of invention under 37 CFR 1.475, the examiner may require applicant, in response to that Office action, to elect the invention to which the claims shall be restricted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a requirement may be made before any action on the merits but may be made at any time before final action at examiner's discretion. Review of such unity requirements is provided under 37 CFR 1.143 and 1.144.
